# ScreenToast

> ScreenToast is a native macOS screen recorder for product demos. It records your screen, then polishes the take automatically: zooms on the clicks that matter, a smoothed cursor, a background and padding, captions transcribed on the Mac, and an optional narration script written from what you did on screen. Recording and editing are free; ScreenToast Pro ($59/year or $7/month) unlocks export. Requires macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon or Intel. Under 10 MB to download. Recordings never leave the Mac.

Key facts:
- Records a display, a window, or an area locked to 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 or 4:3, with camera, microphone and system audio on separate tracks.
- Four zoom types: automatic from clicks, manual, follow-cursor, and a glass loupe. Every zoom is editable on the timeline.
- Edit by transcript, one-click filler-word removal, captions in four styles (including karaoke) and .srt export, all on-device.
- Automatically finds and blurs API keys, tokens, email addresses and card numbers in the recording.
- Camera bubble, side-by-side or camera-only layouts, background removal, colour looks.
- Exports MP4, HEVC, GIF or ProRes, with presets for YouTube, TikTok, Reels, LinkedIn, X, Product Hunt and the web.
- No Windows version. No cloud upload or share links; exports are files.
